JUDGMENT:
(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Sri Rajender Khanna, learned counsel for the appellant- husband and Sri P. Ramachandram, learned counsel for the respondent-wife.

2. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order and decree dated 01.04.2013 in F.C.O.P.No.553 of 2011 passed by learned Family Court-cum-Additional Chief Judge, Secunderabad, the appellant-husband preferred the present appeal.

3. The appellant-husband had filed the aforesaid O.P. against the respondent-wife under Section 13(1) (ia) and Section 26 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, for dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty and visitation rights of his daughter, on the following grounds:-
i. His marriage was performed on 12.02.2003 as per Hindu rites and customs.
 ii. It is an arranged marriage.
 iii. The said marriage was consummated.
iv. They were blessed with a daughter namely Sritha Janasri on 27.05.2005.
v. Initially, the relationship between him and his wife was cordial and peaceful.

Subsequently, the respondent- wife started behaving in a different way and turned to be adamant in her opinion and action, which led to take him separate residence by going away from his parents and others.
vi. On confirming pregnancy, the respondent-wife had abruptly left to her parent's house much earlier than the period when normally pregnant women go to their parents for delivery.

sentences.text: She was not interested in sharing any information with him.
viii. She conceived in the year 2004.
ix. Subsequently, he and his family had been waiting for the invitation from her parents to attend the Cradle ceremony.
x. Surprisingly, there has been no intimation or invitation from her or her parents in any manner.
xi. However, he and his family members were not inclined to blow the said issue disproportionately and patiently tolerated such insult hoping that she will mend her ways.
xii. His mother and sister, though uninvited, went to her house in order to give gifts to her and her child.
However, they were insulted by her and her parents at their house.
Therefore, they left the said house abruptly.
xiii. He tried his level best to get his wife and their child back to his company.
xiv. All the efforts made by him and his family members became futile exercise.
xv. She informed him that she has decided not to join his company and wanted to take divorce.
xvi. She started suspecting his fidelity.
xvii. She and her parents refused him to spend time with his child.
There is no change in her attitude.
She and her parents started making demands like sharing of properties to her to an extent of Rs.10,00,000/- so that she can think about going for a mutual divorce.
xviii.
They have also threatened him that they will implicate him in false criminal cases.
xix. He has filed a petition vide F.C.O.P.No.430 of 2005 seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
The same was dismissed on 26.09.2007.
xx. She started alleging that he is having extra-marital affair.
Therefore, she informed him that she will not stay with him.
xxi. She has also lodged a complaint against him and his family members for the offence under Section 498A of IPC and on the said complaint, C.C.No.411 of 2006 was registered and ended in acquittal.
Thus, she subjected him to cruelty.
Therefore, he has filed the aforesaid petition seeking dissolution of marriage and for visitation rights of his child.

4. The respondent-wife filed counter denying the said allegations with the following grounds:-

sentences.text: She never resorted to any criminal act as alleged by the appellant-husband.
ii. She never demanded any amount, much less Rs.10,00,000/-as alleged by him for obtaining the decree of divorce with mutual consent.
iii. He has filed F.C.O.P.No.430 of 2011 seeking restitution of conjugal rights and the same was dismissed by the learned Family Court.
Even then, there is no change in his attitude.
iv. She was compelled to lodge a complaint against him and his family members.
v. Despite entering into Ex.A5, Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) dated 16.08.2010 and Ex.A6 undertaking, there is no change in his attitude.
Thus, he has filed the aforesaid O.P. with false and baseless allegations only to get rid of her and her daughter.
5. To prove the said cruelty, the appellant-husband examined himself as PW1, his friend as PW2 and his mother as PW3 and filed Exs.A1 to A7 documents.
To disprove the said allegations, the respondent-wife examined herself as RW1 and filed Exs.B1 to B4 documents.
6. On consideration of the entire evidence both oral and documentary, learned Family Court dismissed the O.P. filed by the appellant-husband.
However, visitation rights of his child were granted to him on all 2nd and 4th Sundays from 10:30 AM to 5:00 PM at the respondent-wife's residence.
Learned Family Court also granted liberty to the appellant-husband to make any offer with regard to the maintenance of his child, basing on which the intervals for the visitation can be increased.
7. As discussed supra, the appellant-husband has filed the aforesaid O.P. against the respondent-wife seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.
He has not mentioned any specific instance or specific cruel act against the respondent-wife.
Their marriage was consummated and they were blessed with a baby girl namely Sritha Janasree on 27.05.2005.
She is now 19 years.
She is with her mother.
8. It is also relevant to note that the appellant-husband filed a petition under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking restitution of conjugal rights and the same was dismissed on 26.09.2007.
He did not prefer any appeal.
The said order attained finality.

9. The respondent-wife has lodged a complaint against the appellant-husband and his family members and Police in turn registered a case against the appellant-husband and his family members for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
On completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer laid charge sheet vide C.C.No.411 of 2006 against them.
The same ended in acquittal.
10. As discussed supra, the aforesaid O.P. No.430 of 2005 was dismissed on 26.09.2007.
He has filed the present O.P. on 07.09.2011 i.e. after a lapse of almost four years.

sentences.text: According to the respondent-wife, the appellant-husband maintained illicit relationship with one Benedict Raylenne Maria.
In proof of the same, she has filed Ex.B3 sale deed and Ex.B4 agreement of sale.
She is also accused No.2 in C.C.No.411 of 2006.
However, she was discharged in the said case.
12. Vide Ex.A4 Judgment dated 02.09.2010, the appellant-husband and his family members were acquitted.
The Respondent-wife did not prefer any appeal against the said judgment and has attained finality.

13. Perusal of the record would reveal that disputes arose between the appellant-husband and the respondent-wife on the ground that he is maintaining extra-marital relationship with the aforesaid Maria.
Therefore, negotiations were held between them.
They came to an understanding on certain terms and the same were reduced in writing vide Ex.A5, MOU dated 16.08.2010.
The appellant-husband, his brothers, sisters and mother undertook to look after the respondent- wife well and they will not create any problems in future.
The appellant-husband agreed that he will not sell and alienate his share of properties without the consent of the respondent-wife.
The appellant- husband agreed that he will not entertain third parties (women) in his marital life with the respondent-wife.
The Respondent-wife also agreed that she will cooperate with the appellant-husband for smooth living without any dispute with regard to marital life.
If the agreement is violated, the respondent-wife has right to approach the court of law for the remedies available to her as per law.

The appellant-husband, his brother, his sisters and his mother signed the said MOU.
14.
Thereafter, a written assurance dated 12.10.2003 Ex.A6 was given by the appellant-husband stating that he will take care of the respondent-wife and her daughter properly.
The appellant-husband agreed to stay with the respondent-wife as per her will, till she and her parents get confidence in him.
He has agreed that he will not create any problem and he will take care of the welfare of the respondent- wife and his daughter.

Despite the said agreement and undertaking,
according to the respondent-wife, the appellant-husband disobeyed the same.
ExA7 is the order dated 06.06.2012 in I.A.No.553 of 2012 in I.A.No.1527 of 2010 in O.S.No.1349 of 2010.
The appellant-husband herein is respondent No.8.
The said order would reveal that there are disputes with regard to properties of the appellant-husband.
15. The appellant-husband(PW1), during his cross-examination
categorically admitted that said Maria is his vendee and he did not have any acquaintance with her prior to the said transaction.
However, he has denied to a suggestion that he used to meet her regularly at Jalaja computers.
16. He has also denied to a suggestion that he has informed the respondent-wife that he has already married the said Maria earlier and he has cheated the respondent-wife.
He was Director of Leo Meridian Resort.
He is partner in Jalaja Computers.
He has admitted about entering of the said Exs.A5 MOU and A6 undertaking.
But according to him, the same were obtained forcefully without his free will.

sentences.text: As discussed supra, he is a business man.
He is partner of Jalaja Computers and also was Director of Leo Meridian Resort.
Therefore, the question of obtaining the said Exs.A5 and A6 forcefully by the respondent-wife does not arise.
He has not lodged any complaint with the Police or brought the said fact to the notice of elders.
The said fact would reveal that he has made the said allegations only to suit his convenience.

During cross-examination, he has further admitted that he has stayed with the respondent-wife and at that particular point of time, she has withdrawn the criminal case against him.
18. PW2, his friend during cross-examination categorically admitted that he is into real-estate business since last past ten years.
He has business transactions with the appellant-husband.
He is working on commission basis.
The marriage of the appellant-husband and the respondent-wife was performed at Chiran Court Club.
The contents of third paragraph of his chief affidavit are false as the appellant-husband(PW1) requested him to sign on the chief affidavit.
Therefore, the said fact would reveal that the appellant-husband examined PW2, his friend, to prove the cruelty.
The evidence of PW2 is not useful.
19. PW3, mother of the appellant-husband(PW1), during cross- examination categorically admitted that she is party to Ex.A6 and she knows the contents.
The respondent-wife(RW1) filed a criminal case against PW1, PW3 and eight others.
Prior to its withdrawal, PW1 used to stay at RW1's house.
She withdrew the said case.
After withdrawing the said case PW1 stayed for two years at RW1's house.
She has no objection for both the parties living together or living separately.
She did not know the name of PW1's daughter.

20. The afore-stated facts would reveal that though the appellant- husband filed the aforesaid O.P.
against the respondent-wife seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty, he has not mentioned any specific instance or specific cruel act said to have been resorted by the respondent-wife.
All the said issues are petty issues.
They can be resolved by negotiations.
The respondent-wife is working as MPDO as on the date of filing of the said O.P. They were blessed with a daughter namely Shritha Janasri on 27.05.2005.
She is 19 years as on today.
Parties instead of living their normal life, fighting for dissolution of marriage and it is ego fight.
Though visitation rights were granted to the appellant-husband, he has not availed the same.

21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Samar Ghosh vs. Jaya Ghosh1 relying on its earlier judgment in Naveen Kohli vs. Neelu Kohli 2 observed certain incidents of cruelty in paragraph No.101 which are as under:-
101.
No uniform standard can ever be laid down for guidance, yet we deem it appropriate to enumerate some instances of human behaviour which may be relevant in dealing with the cases of "mental cruelty".

The instances indicated in the succeeding paragraphs are only illustrative and not exhaustive:
(i) On consideration of complete matrimonial life of the parties, acute mental pain,
agony and suffering as would not make possible for the parties to live with each other could come within the broad parameters of mental cruelty.

5

(ii) On comprehensive appraisal of the entire matrimonial life of the parties, it becomes abundantly clear that situation is such that the (2007) 4 SCC 511 (2006) 4 SCC 558 wronged party cannot reasonably be asked to put up with such conduct and continue to live with other party.

(iii) Mere coldness or lack of affection cannot amount to cruelty, frequent rudeness of language, petulance of manner, indifference and neglect may reach such a degree that it makes the married life for the other spouse absolutely intolerable.
(iv) Mental cruelty is a state of mind.

The feeling of deep anguish, disappointment,
frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of other for a long time may lead to mental cruelty.

(v) A sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment calculated to torture,
discommode or render miserable life of the spouse.
(vi) Sustained unjustifiable conduct and behaviour of one spouse actually affecting physical and mental health of the other spouse.

The treatment complained of and the resultant danger or apprehension must be very grave,
substantial and weighty.

(vii) Sustained reprehensible conduct, studied neglect, indifference or total departure from the normal standard of conjugal kindness causing injury to mental health or deriving sadistic pleasure can also amount to mental cruelty.

(viii) The conduct must be much more than jealousy, selfishness, possessiveness, which causes unhappiness and dissatisfaction and emotional upset may not be a ground for grant of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.
(ix) Mere trivial irritations, quarrels, normal wear and tear of the married life which happens in day-to-day life would not be adequate for grant of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.
(x) The married life should be reviewed as a whole and a few isolated instances over a period of years will not amount to cruelty.

The ill conduct must be persistent for a fairly lengthy period, where the relationship has deteriorated to an extent that because of the acts and behaviour of a spouse, the wronged party finds it extremely difficult to live with the other party any longer, may amount to mental cruelty.

(xi) If a husband submits himself for an operation of sterilisation without medical reasons and without the consent or knowledge of his wife and similarly, if the wife undergoes vasectomy or abortion without medical reason or without the consent or knowledge of her husband, such an act of the spouse may lead to mental cruelty.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (xii) Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
(xiii) Unilateral decision of either husband or wife after marriage not to have child from the marriage may amount to cruelty.
(xiv) Where there has been a long period of continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair.
The marriage becomes a fiction though supported by a legal tie.
By refusing to sever that tie, the law in such cases, does not serve the sanctity of marriage; on the contrary, it shows scant regard for the feelings and emotions of the parties.
In such like situations, it may lead to mental cruelty.

22. Learned counsel for the respondent-wife placed reliance on the principle laid down by the apex court in Darshan Gupta v. Radhika Gupta 3 to contend that the allegation made by the appellant-husband seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty does not amount cruelty.
23. In the light of the same, as discussed supra, the appellant- husband herein failed to prove the said cruelty.
On consideration of entire evidence, both oral and documentary, learned Family Court dismissed the O.P. filed by the appellant-husband seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.
However, visitation rights of the daughter were granted to him.

Now she attained majority,
it is for her to take a decision whether to meet the appellant-husband or stay with him or to stay with her mother.
24. The impugned order is a reasoned order and well-founded.
It does not require interference by this Court in the present appeal.
The appellant-husband failed to make out any case to interfere with the said order.
It is liable to be dismissed and accordingly it is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
